author: Hesychius of Jerusalem
occasion: Delivered for the feast of Pascha (Easter) to proclaim the resurrection of Christ and its cosmic significance.
argument: The homily opens with a holy royal trumpet that has gathered a spiritual theater: Bethlehem filled the trumpet and Zion fired it; in it the Cross is the hammer and the Resurrection the anvil. Hesychius confesses he cannot utter the beauty, light, joy, and kingdom of this trumpet, and asks how to greet the tomb that begets life. He insists the one subject — the incarnate Word — truly suffers in the flesh and works miracles in his divinity, yet the two are inseparably woven together. The same Christ who descended into Hades as dead freed the dead as God; angels serve at the tomb and announce the resurrection to the women, a proclamation that surpasses all prophecy. He then cites Hosea 6:1-2 and Isaiah 33:9-10 to show the resurrection fulfills Scripture: the Lord now rises when he raises Adam, now is glorified when he establishes impassibility for the nations, now is exalted when he lifts the servant-form to heaven and the cherubic throne, and the types cease while the truth blooms, to the shame of unbelieving opponents.

outline.move: Introduces the Paschal feast through the image of a holy royal trumpet gathering a spiritual theater; Bethlehem filled it, Zion fired it; the Cross is hammer, the Resurrection anvil; the homilist despairs of expressing its beauty, light, joy, and kingdom, and asks how to greet the life-giving tomb.

Affirms the unity of Christ: the same one who died as man conquered death as God; his flesh serves the passions, his divinity the signs, yet they are indivisible; Joseph buried him as dead, soldiers guarded him as dead, but the gatekeepers of Hades cowered seeing him as God.

Describes Christ's descent into Hades freeing the dead; angels minister at the tomb and appear to the women in shining garments, announcing the risen Jesus of Nazareth; the angel's word exceeds prophetic interpretation; Hosea 6:1-2 and the beginning of Isaiah 33 are quoted.

Completes the Isaiah quotation (LXX Isa 33:9-10); the homilist explicates each 'now' of the Lord's first-person oracle: raising Adam, granting impassibility to the nations, exalting the servant-form to the cherubic throne, ending the types, blooming the truth, shaming opponents; closes with a Trinitarian doxology.

cast.name: Christ (the Word Incarnate)
cast.who: The one subject of the homily, fully God and fully man, who suffers, dies, descends to Hades, rises, and is exalted.

cast.name: Joseph
cast.who: Buried Jesus, treating him as dead.

cast.name: The Soldiers
cast.who: Guarded the tomb, treating Jesus as a dead man.

cast.name: The Angels
cast.who: Ministered at the tomb; appeared to the women in shining garments and announced the resurrection.

cast.name: The Gatekeepers of Hades
cast.who: Saw Christ as God and cowered in fear.

cast.name: The Women
cast.who: Came to the tomb weeping, seeking the crucified Jesus; received the angelic message.

cast.name: Hosea
cast.who: Prophet cited for the third-day resurrection (Hos 6:1-2).

cast.name: Isaiah
cast.who: Prophet cited for the shame of Lebanon/Sharon and the Lord's rising, glorification, and exaltation (LXX Isa 33:9-10).

cast.name: Adam
cast.who: The first man, fallen by transgression, now raised by Christ's resurrection.

cast.name: The Jews
cast.who: Opponents addressed in Isaiah's prophecy, put to shame by the resurrection.

voices.speaker: Hesychius (homilist)
voices.how_marked: First-person narration and rhetorical questions; direct address to congregation.

voices.speaker: Angel at the tomb
voices.how_marked: Direct quotation introduced by πῶς δὲ πρὸς αὐτὰς ἔλεγον and closing with καθὼς εἶπεν αὐτός.

voices.speaker: Hosea (Scripture)
voices.how_marked: Quoted as prophecy: Ὡσηὲ τὸν καιρὸν τῆς ἀναστάσεως λέγει ... Ταῦτα μὲν γὰρ Ὡσηὲ προφητείας τὰ ῥήματα.

voices.speaker: Isaiah (Scripture)
voices.how_marked: Quoted as prophecy: Ἠσαΐας οἶδεν ... Ἀκουε πάλιν ποῖα Ἠσαΐας ἐσάλπισεν.

voices.speaker: The Lord (Christ speaking in Isaiah quotation)
voices.how_marked: First-person prophetic utterance within the Isaiah quotation: νῦν ἀναστήσομαι, λέγει κύριος ... νῦν αἰσχυνθήσεσθε.

voices.speaker: The Lord (Christ, in homilist's exposition)
voices.how_marked: Homilist paraphrases each 'now' clause in the Lord's voice: νῦν ἀναστήσομαι ὅταν ἐγείρω τὸν Ἀδὰμ ...

key_terms.sense: The Christian feast of Easter, celebrating Christ's passion and resurrection.
The eternal Word of God become incarnate, the single subject of Christ's human and divine actions.
Christ's rising from the dead, which liberates humanity and fulfills prophecy.
The realm of the dead into which Christ descended to free the souls held there.
The sufferings of Christ in the flesh (passion, death), truly undergone by the incarnate Word.
The mighty works and signs displaying Christ's divine power, inseparable from his passion.
Incorruptibility, the state of glorified life granted through the resurrection.
Impassibility, the freedom from suffering and death conferred on humanity through the risen Christ.
The 'form of a servant' (Phil 2:7) — Christ's assumed humanity, now exalted to heaven.
Old Testament types and shadows that cease when the reality (Christ) appears.
The true reality fulfilled in Christ, contrasted with the types of the Law.

scripture: The author cites the Greek Septuagint (LXX). Hosea 6:1-2 is quoted (LXX Hos 6:1-2 = MT Hos 6:1-2). The Isaiah quotation matches LXX Isaiah 33:9-10 (Lebanon, Sharon, Galilee, Carmel, 'Now I will rise'). Isaiah 35:2 is not clearly quoted. Psalm numbering follows the LXX (which differs from Hebrew by -1 after Ps 8). In modern citations, use standard versification: Hosea 6:1-2; Isaiah 33:9-10.
uncertain: Exact date of delivery within Hesychius' episcopate (c. 412–451)
Whether this homily was preached in Jerusalem or another setting
Precise manuscript tradition beyond the cited Sinaiticus gr. 492
Whether the Isaiah quotation includes material from Isaiah 35:2

_unresolved_facts.claim: to proclaim the resurrection of Christ and its cosmic significance
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Σάλπιγξ ἡμῖν ἱερὰ καὶ βασιλικὴ τὸ πνευματικὸν τοῦτο συνεκρότησεν θέατρον
_unresolved_facts.fix: Delivered for the holy Pascha to proclaim the resurrection. It stresses the unity of the incarnate Word, Christ's freeing of the dead in Hades, and the fulfilment of prophecy. It never speaks of 'cosmic significance'.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Isaiah 33:9-10 ... the Lord now rises ... now is glorified ... now is exalted ... shame of unbelieving opponents
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Νῦν ἀναστήσομαι, λέγει κύριος, νῦν δοξασθήσομαι, νῦν ὑψωθήσομαι. Νῦν ὄψεσθε, νῦν αἰσχυνθήσεσθε.
_unresolved_facts.fix: The quoted LXX text runs from 33:9 (Lebanon, Sharon, Galilee, Carmel) through the 'now' oracle, which in LXX numbering extends into 33:11. Cite it as Isaiah 33:9-11 (LXX). In the MT the 'Now I will rise' words are 33:10. Also say the opponents are the Jews, to whom the homilist says the word is addressed (Πρὸς γὰρ τοὺς Ἰουδαίους).

_unresolved_facts.claim: Joseph buried him as dead, soldiers guarded him as dead, but the gatekeepers of Hades cowered seeing him as God. (placed in u01-rem-early)
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ὡς νεκρὸν αὐτὸν Ἰωσὴφ ἐκήδευσεν, ἀλλ' ὁ κηδευθεὶς ὡς
_unresolved_facts.fix: The Joseph clause begins at the end of u01-open and carries over mid-sentence into u01-rem-early. The soldiers and gatekeepers are in u01-rem-early.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Direct quotation introduced by πῶς δὲ πρὸς αὐτὰς ἔλεγον and closing with καθὼς εἶπεν αὐτός.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Τουτέστιν οὐρανὸς αὐτῷ τόπος, ἐκεῖ τὰ μύρα πέμψατε. Ἠγέρθη, οὐχ ἡμεῖς αὐτὸν ἠγείραμεν. Ὑμῶν ἕνεκα τὸν λίθον ἐκυλίσαμεν
_unresolved_facts.fix: The angels' speech opens with the Matthean words (Ἰησοῦν ζητεῖτε ... ἠγέρθη γὰρ καθὼς εἶπεν). The homilist then expands it in the angels' voice, with several angels speaking ('ἐκυλίσαμεν'). The source reads πὼς, and the speech ends at 'Ἠγέρθη, καθὼς εἶπεν αὐτός.'
